title: Quick check: Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs”?
options: The browser will infer all application behavior even if inputs and state are contradictory.
The concept allows application code to mutate React-managed DOM and state directly.
Roles and semantics should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
The concept removes the need to consider error states or accessibility.
questions.answer_key: Roles and semantics should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs: Roles and semantics should use semantics and focus/keyboard behavior that assistive technology can observe.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most reliable when applying Roles and semantics?
options: Optimize by adding every available Hook without measuring the result.
Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
Skip validation because a successful render proves that the application is correct.
Store duplicate copies of every value so each component can change it independently.
questions.answer_key: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs: Test keyboard use, accessible names, focus order, and semantic controls.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before considering “Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs” complete?
options: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
Check only whether the file exists; syntax and runtime behavior do not matter.
Assume a client-side check proves that a remote service accepted the change.
Rely only on a screenshot of the happy path and never repeat the test.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is grounded in Accessible Dialogs, Menus, and Tabs: Verify the documented result with a normal example and at least one boundary, loading, or failure case.
